name: ROYAL READING
clue: Ordered at the 1604 Hampton Court Conference, this translation of scripture appeared in 1611 and gave us 'the skin of my teeth'
response: the King James Bible (King James Version)

name: A PLACE IN THE NAME
clue: Her sister Parthenope was named for Naples, and this founder of modern nursing likewise got her name from her Italian birthplace

name: DOUBLE-0 ONCE
clue: This Australian model played James Bond once, in 1969's 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service,' then walked away from the role

name: GREAT EXPECTATIONS
clue: Born a minor German princess named Sophie, she took Russia's throne from her own husband in a 1762 coup

name: SHAKESPEARE'S ROMANS
clue: Banished by the Rome he had saved, this general leads an enemy army to its gates in the Shakespeare tragedy bearing his name

name: THE PERIODIC TABLE
clue: Element 98, first made in 1950 in a university cyclotron, is named for the state where it was created

name: BARRIER TO ENTRY
clue: This Manhattan thoroughfare of finance was named for a wooden palisade the Dutch raised in 1653 to protect New Amsterdam

name: SCANDALOUS PREMIERES
clue: The audience brawled at the 1913 Paris premiere of this Stravinsky ballet about a maiden who dances herself to death

name: SEVEN WONDERS
clue: The oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is also the only one still largely standing

name: ONCE IN A LIFETIME
clue: Mark Twain arrived 2 weeks after its 1835 appearance and, just as he predicted, left with it the day after its 1910 return

name: RUN FOR THE AGES
clue: Running barefoot, this Ethiopian palace guard won the 1960 Rome Olympic marathon, then wore shoes to win again in Tokyo

name: CROSS PURPOSES
clue: Honoring founder Henry Dunant's homeland, the Red Cross flag reverses the colors of this country's square national banner

name: HIGH & DRY
clue: Astronomers prize the cloudless skies above this Chilean region, Earth's driest non-polar place and home to the ALMA observatory

name: AT THE OPERA
clue: Puccini died before finishing this opera, so at its 1926 premiere Toscanini laid down his baton where the composer had stopped

name: INITIAL HERE
clue: A congressman's slip on his West Point paperwork gave this Ohio-born Union commander and future president the initials 'U.S.'

name: LOGO LEGENDS
clue: The dribbling silhouette in the NBA's logo was modeled on this Lakers guard nicknamed 'Mr. Clutch'

name: DOUBLE LAUREATES
clue: The only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, this American chemist took Chemistry in 1954 and Peace in 1962

name: BACK FROM THE DEAD
clue: Revived from prayer books into everyday speech, this ancient language has been an official tongue of Israel since 1948

name: ANCIENT GAME NIGHT
clue: Called weiqi in China and baduk in Korea, this territorial board game defied computers until AlphaGo's landmark 2016 victory

name: HOME COURT ADVANTAGE
clue: The Flushing Meadows home of tennis's US Open is named for this champion, who won 1973's 'Battle of the Sexes'

name: DEMOTION COMMOTION
clue: An 11-year-old English schoolgirl named this world discovered in 1930, and its P-L symbol also honors Percival Lowell

name: FAB FOUR SOLO
clue: Though credited to the Beatles, this 1965 ballad features only Paul McCartney and a string quartet

name: POSTHUMOUS POETS
clue: Fewer than a dozen of her poems saw print before her death in Amherst in 1886, and nearly 1,800 surfaced afterward

name: SWAN SONGS
clue: Dead at 35 in 1791, this Salzburg-born prodigy left his Requiem unfinished, and his pupil Süssmayr completed the mass

name: LONG LIVE THE KING
clue: Becoming king at age 4, this French monarch reigned 72 years, outliving both his son and his grandson

name: RING RECORDS
clue: In 1956 this heavyweight champion hung up his gloves at 49-0, having knocked out 43 of the 49 men he faced

name: PEN NAMES
clue: This Missouri-born river pilot took his pen name from a leadsman's cry meaning two fathoms, or 12 feet, of safe water

name: ACCIDENTAL PRESIDENTS
clue: He's the only person to serve as both U.S. vice president and president without being elected to either office

name: MIDDLE OF NOWHERE
clue: Named for a Jules Verne captain, this oceanic 'pole of inaccessibility' is where space agencies aim their dying spacecraft

name: GODS ON THE CALENDAR
clue: Looking backward and forward at once, the two-faced Roman god of doorways and beginnings gave his name to this month
